paper.citation: Azriel, D., Brown, L. D., Sklar, M., Berk, R., Buja, A. and Zhao, L. (2022). Semi-Supervised Linear Regression. JASA 117(540), 2238–2251.
paper.title: Semi-Supervised Linear Regression
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_version: arXiv:1612.02391v4, 13 April 2021; version linked by the first author under the published JASA article
paper.source_locator: Section 5.1, equation (27), PDF p. 18; Figure 1, PDF p. 19 (alpha=1/2, beta=1, n=100, m=2n); Section 1.1 and Section 2 define sampling and projection.

mechanism.name: Best linear slope under a quadratic Gaussian response
generation_equations: Two independent samples from the same population: source_n_labeled rows with observed Y and source_n_unlabeled rows with observed X only. R=1 in the first labeled block; Y_obs=Y there. R=0 in the remaining block; Y_obs=0 is a placeholder.

sampling.dependence: Independent rows, with within-row dependence specified by the equations.
sampling.predictor_provenance: The generator exposes covariates as auxiliary information; fitted predictions are supplied by subsequent statistical methods using permitted labeled data and their documented training or cross-fitting splits. This contribution supplies the sampling law and observed data; later methods specify training and validation partitions. Prediction columns are absent.

assumptions: Independent sampling units; labeled and unlabeled samples are independent draws from the same joint/marginal population.
Label availability is fixed by sampling design independently of generated values, corresponding to MCAR sampling.
The stated distributions, independence conditions and selected population functional define the target. Its numerical verification applies to the declared scenario.

properties.notes: One active covariate; a quadratic conditional mean with a linear-projection target. effective_dimension counts inputs that determine the conditional response law, including an observed surrogate or the sole tail-dependent auxiliary variable; correlated extra coordinates may carry additional information. high_dimensional compares total dimension with source labeled sample size. Interactions marks a nonadditive response/probability map.

estimand.name: beta_L2
estimand.definition: Slope in the population least-squares projection of Y on (1,X).

truth.expression: Slope in the population least-squares projection of Y on (1,X).
truth.derivation: Cov(X,Y)/Var(X)=[0.5 E(X^3)+E(X^2)]/1=1; the projection intercept is 0.5.

adaptations: Select alpha=1/2 and n=100 from the source Figure 1 grid, beta=1 and m=2n.
Return the slope component of the population linear projection through the scalar truth interface.
Represent independent labeled/unlabeled samples in a single table: all X columns, label indicator R and Y_obs. A zero on an R=0 row is a finite placeholder.
The generate argument n counts total rows. Source total yields exact source allocation; other n use nearest-integer ratio allocation with both groups nonempty.
Use local PCG64 random streams, with independent covariate and response-noise streams. Each row remains an independent population draw.
warnings: No explicit latent-variable metadata or reliably identifiable latent declarations; absence from this list does not prove that no latent variables exist.
